title: 12 Metal Musicians Who Survived Near-Death Experiences

content:
Rock and roll has always lived close to the edge. Pyro, drugs, fast cars and dangerous stage stunts have claimed more than their share of musicians over the years.

But some of rock’s biggest names went right up to the edge and came back. One says he was declared dead and turned it into a hit. Another was set on fire in front of a stadium crowd. A third lost his arm at 21 and kept on drumming.

Here are 12 rock and metal legends who cheated death, and what they said about it afterward.

Contents

  • 1. Nikki Sixx (Mötley Crüe)
  • 2. James Hetfield (Metallica)
  • 3. Ozzy Osbourne
  • 4. Slash (Guns N’ Roses)
  • 5. Alice Cooper
  • 6. Bret Michaels (Poison)
  • 7. Ace Frehley (KISS)
  • 8. Phil Anselmo (Pantera)
  • 9. Frank Zappa
  • 10. Brian May (Queen)
  • 11. Keith Richards (The Rolling Stones)
  • 12. Rick Allen (Def Leppard)

1. Nikki Sixx (Mötley Crüe)

On Dec. 23, 1987, after a long night of partying in Los Angeles, Mötley Crüe bassist Nikki Sixx overdosed on heroin. By his own account, he was declared dead for two minutes before paramedics brought him back with two shots of adrenaline. Guns N’ Roses drummer Steven Adler, who was there, tells it differently: he says he revived Sixx himself.

Either way, Sixx says he pulled out his tubes, walked out of the hospital and went home. Asked by Rolling Stone in 2019 what dying had taught him, he said: “That it hurts to come back.”

The overdose inspired “Kickstart My Heart,” one of Mötley Crüe’s biggest hits, on 1989’s Dr. Feelgood. He went to rehab soon after.

How close it came: Declared dead for two minutes, by his own account.

On Aug. 8, 1992, Metallica were co-headlining Montreal’s Olympic Stadium with Guns N’ Roses. At the start of “Fade to Black,” James Hetfield walked into the path of a pyro blast.

“A big coloured flame goes right up under me. I’m burnt,” he later recalled on VH1’s Behind the Music. He suffered second- and third-degree burns on his arms and a deep burn on his left hand. “My hand looked the worst. It bubbled up in two layers that came off,” he said.

Metallica’s set ended there, and the night ended in a riot after Guns N’ Roses cut their own set short. Hetfield was back 17 days later, singing with his arm bandaged while Metal Church’s John Marshall played rhythm guitar for the rest of the tour.

How close it came: According to bassist Jason Newsted, “If he had been breathing in, he would have been dead.”

3. Ozzy Osbourne

On Dec. 8, 2003, Ozzy Osbourne flipped a quad bike on his estate in Buckinghamshire, England, and it landed on top of him. He broke his collarbone, eight ribs and a vertebra in his neck.

Sharon said he stopped breathing and had no pulse. His bodyguard, Sam Ruston, gave him mouth-to-mouth. “He had to bring me back to life twice,” Ozzy said a few weeks later. “If it wasn’t for Sam I probably wouldn’t be here.” He spent eight days in a medically induced coma.

It wasn’t his first brush with death. In March 1982, he was asleep on his tour bus when a small plane buzzed it, clipped it and crashed, killing his guitarist, Randy Rhoads. Ozzy died on July 22, 2025, at 76, just weeks after his farewell show in Birmingham.

How close it came: No pulse, and brought back twice, in Ozzy’s words.

4. Slash (Guns N’ Roses)

In the early 1990s, at the height of Guns N’ Roses’ fame, Slash overdosed on heroin and cocaine in a San Francisco hotel. He collapsed in the hallway after asking a maid where the elevator was.

By his own account, he was out for eight minutes. “They told me later that I died,” he said years later.

He woke up in the hospital and, as he put it, “checked myself out because we had a show the next night.”

How close it came: Out for eight minutes, by his own count.

5. Alice Cooper

Alice Cooper has been “executing” himself on stage for decades. In the ’80s, he did it on the gallows, with a harness and a thick piano wire keeping the noose about an inch from his neck. The stunt was designed by magician James Randi.

In 1988, during a rehearsal in London, the wire he had never replaced finally snapped. “The wire snaps. I could hear the rope hit my chin,” he told Entertainment Weekly in 2018. “If it caught my chin it would have been a different result.”

He escaped with a rope burn and blacked out, but he still played the gig. Then he switched to a stronger wire and kept the hanging in the show.

How close it came: One snapped wire away from a real hanging.

6. Bret Michaels (Poison)

Bret Michaels had a year from hell. At the Tony Awards in June 2009, a piece of falling scenery hit him in the head and broke his nose. In April 2010, he needed an emergency appendectomy.

Ten days later, he had a subarachnoid hemorrhage, bleeding at the base of his brain. “It sounded like a small handgun went off in the back of my head,” he told Oprah. He spent about 10 days in intensive care, and his neurosurgeon called him “a very lucky person.”

Weeks later, he was back in the hospital with numbness on his left side, and doctors found a hole in his heart he’d had since birth. He still went on to win NBC’s Celebrity Apprentice that spring. “It just wasn’t my time yet,” he said.

How close it came: Subarachnoid hemorrhages kill about 15% of victims before they reach a hospital.

7. Ace Frehley (KISS)

On Dec. 12, 1976, KISS opened their show at the Lakeland Civic Center in Florida with “Detroit Rock City.” As Ace Frehley came down the stairs from the top of the set, he grabbed a metal rail that was live because of a grounding fault.

The current ran through him and his guitar, and at first he couldn’t let go. “If I hadn’t been able to let go, I would have died,” he told the Lakeland Ledger. The road crew dragged him off the stairs.

After about 10 minutes in the dressing room, he came back to a standing ovation and finished the show. His bandmates told him to write a song about it, and he did: “Shock Me,” his first lead vocal on a KISS album. Ace died on Oct. 16, 2025, at 74, after a fall at home.

How close it came: “I should have been dead that night,” he told MusicRadar.

8. Phil Anselmo (Pantera)

On July 13, 1996, right after a Pantera show in Dallas, Phil Anselmo overdosed on heroin backstage. Friends spent about 20 minutes trying to revive him, and he woke up in the back of an ambulance.

Four days later, he issued a statement owning up to it, saying he had “died for four to five minutes.” “There was no lights, no beautiful music, just nothing,” he added.

He has said he turned to heroin to cope with severe back pain. Twenty years later, he told Decibel: “It’s amazing I came back from it alive.”

How close it came: “Died for four to five minutes,” in his own words.

9. Frank Zappa

Frank Zappa had the worst week of his career in December 1971. On Dec. 4, he and the Mothers of Invention were playing the Casino de Montreux in Switzerland when a fan fired a flare gun into the ceiling. The casino burned to the ground, and the band’s gear went with it. Deep Purple, in town to record an album, watched it burn and wrote “Smoke on the Water” about it.

Six days later, at London’s Rainbow Theatre, a man from the audience pushed Zappa off the stage into the concrete orchestra pit, a drop of about 12 feet. “The band thought I was dead,” Zappa wrote in his 1989 memoir. He had a fractured leg, a broken rib, a head wound and a crushed larynx.

He spent a long stretch in a wheelchair and then a leg brace, and was off the road for most of a year. The injuries permanently lowered his voice and left one leg shorter than the other.

How close it came: A fire and a fall into a concrete pit, six days apart.

10. Brian May (Queen)

In May 2020, Brian May was laid up after tearing a muscle in his backside while gardening. Then came 40 minutes of chest pain. It turned out to be what he called “a small heart attack,” and doctors found three clogged arteries.

He had three stents fitted. “I was actually very near death because of this,” he told fans in a video. “I could have died from the blockages that were there.”

In 2024, at 77, he had a minor stroke that left him unable to control one arm for a while. “I didn’t have any control over this arm,” he said. Within about a week, he could play guitar again.

How close it came: Three clogged arteries, and a heart attack he called “small.”

11. Keith Richards (The Rolling Stones)

Keith Richards has survived just about everything, but in 2006, a tree nearly got him. On holiday in Fiji in late April, he lost his grip on a low branch about seven feet up and hit his head on the trunk.

It wasn’t a coconut tree, whatever the headlines said. “Forget any palm tree,” he wrote in his 2010 memoir, Life. But the fall caused bleeding inside his skull, and in early May he had brain surgery in Auckland, New Zealand. According to his surgeon, he woke up right afterward and said, “God, that’s better!”

He was back on stage in Milan that July, where fans waved inflatable palm trees. “I fall out of a tree, they give me one,” he joked.

How close it came: Emergency brain surgery at 62.

12. Rick Allen (Def Leppard)

On New Year’s Eve 1984, Def Leppard drummer Rick Allen crashed his Corvette on the A57 near Sheffield, England. He was 21. The car went through a stone wall, he was thrown out, and his left arm was torn off.

Doctors reattached it, but it had to be removed days later because of infection. Allen later recalled seeing the crash scene from above: “I remember being above the ambulance and observing the whole scene.”

He didn’t quit. With a custom electronic kit that let his feet play what his left arm used to, he played a handful of warm-up gigs in Ireland, then made his big comeback at the Monsters of Rock festival at Castle Donington on Aug. 16, 1986. When Joe Elliott introduced him, “the roar of the crowd was so loud, I burst into tears,” Allen wrote. He’s still Def Leppard’s drummer today.

How close it came: He lost an arm, and nearly his life, at 21.
